message.content: Painting the Eiffel Tower is a fairly routine but meticulous job. In practice, the tower’s maintenance team spends roughly **two weeks** (sometimes up to a month) covering the structure with fresh protective paint. That interval is part of the tower’s scheduled upkeep—every seven years the whole lattice is stripped, cleaned, primed, and then given a new coat of paint to keep the iron from rusting.
